name: Sasa Polyester
desc: Turkish integrated producer of polyester fibres, filaments, PTA and PET chemicals for textile and packaging makers.
markets: Industrial customers in Turkey and export markets in Europe; expansion plans not confirmed.
rationale: B2B polymer producer without a consumer brand; F1 could serve hospitality, but fit is weak.

name: Silmaasema
desc: Finnish optical retailer and eye care provider operating Silmaasema stores and eye clinics.
markets: Customers in Finland through stores and clinics; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Finnish optical chain with local consumer reach; limited international marketing scope makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Mitra Adiperkasa
desc: Indonesian retailer operating licensed lifestyle, fashion, sports and food brands through stores across Indonesia.
markets: Stores across Indonesia carrying licensed international brands; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Large Indonesian retailer with many consumer brands and mall presence; F1 offers local lifestyle exposure, with a franchise tie to an F1 partner.
f1: Franchise operator of Marks & Spencer in Indonesia (M&S is an F1 partner)

name: Genesco
desc: US specialty retailer of footwear and accessories operating Journeys, Schuh and Johnston & Murphy.
markets: Stores and online sales in the US, Canada, the UK and Ireland through Journeys, Schuh and Johnston & Murphy.
rationale: Footwear retail group with youth and sneaker audience across two regions; F1 fan-apparel tie-ins plausible.

name: La Chapelle
desc: Chinese women's fashion retailer selling affordable trendy clothing through stores and online.
markets: Stores and online sales in China; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic Chinese fashion chain aimed at young women; F1 audience overlap is partial and reach is domestic.

name: KPR Mill
desc: Indian vertically integrated textile and apparel group making yarn, fabric and garments, with sugar and ethanol operations.
markets: Supplies yarn and garments to brands in India and export markets including the US and Europe.
rationale: B2B textile maker with little consumer visibility; F1 hospitality could help buyer relationships, but fit is weak.

name: Monte Carlo Fashions
desc: Indian apparel company known for woollen knitwear and cotton clothing sold under the Monte Carlo brand.
markets: Stores and distribution across India; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Indian apparel brand with domestic customers; limited international marketing scope makes F1 a weak fit.

name: Koton
desc: Turkish fashion retailer selling affordable ready-to-wear clothing for women, men and children through stores and online.
markets: Stores in Turkey and in countries across Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia, plus online sales.
rationale: Turkish fashion chain with international store network and Istanbul Grand Prix heritage; F1 offers fan-lifestyle exposure.

name: Lamoda
desc: Russian online fashion and lifestyle retailer selling clothes, shoes and accessories to consumers.
markets: Customers in Russia through its website and app; formerly part of Global Fashion Group.
rationale: Russian online retailer; F1 has had no Russian race since 2022, so an F1 partnership is not realistic.
changed: Divested by Global Fashion Group in 2022

name: American Apparel
desc: Los Angeles clothing brand known for basic garments, now selling blank and branded apparel under Gildan ownership.
markets: Sells mainly online and wholesale in North America; the former store chain was closed after bankruptcy.
rationale: Former high-street brand now a Gildan wholesale label; no independent marketing budget and weak F1 fit.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2015 and 2016; brand acquired by Gildan in 2017

name: New Look Vision Group
desc: Canadian eyecare retailer owning optical store banners such as New Look Eyewear, Iris and Vogue Optical.
markets: Stores and franchises across Canada, concentrated in Quebec and Ontario; no international operations.
rationale: Canadian optical chain with a domestic consumer base; limited relevance to F1.
changed: Taken private after its TSX listing

name: Redbubble
desc: Australian online marketplace where independent artists sell designs printed on apparel, homewares and accessories.
markets: Customers in the United States, Europe and Australia through its Redbubble and TeePublic marketplaces.
rationale: Artist marketplace with global online audience; F1 fan-art and merchandise tie-ins are plausible, though marketing budget is limited.
changed: Parent renamed Articore Group in 2023

name: Brown-Forman
desc: US spirits and wine company behind Jack Daniel's, Woodford Reserve and Old Forester whiskies, selling worldwide.
markets: Sells in more than 170 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global spirits group with brand-led marketing; its Jack Daniel's brand already partners with F1, so fit is direct.
f1: Jack Daniel's is a current F1 partner

name: Anheuser-Busch InBev
desc: World's largest brewer, making Budweiser, Corona and Stella Artois beers sold in markets worldwide.
markets: Operates breweries and sells beer across North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global beer group with sponsorship-led marketing; rival brewer Heineken is already an F1 partner, so category interest is clear.

name: ThaiBeverage
desc: Thai alcohol and beverage group owning Chang beer, Sangsom rum, Mekhong whisky and Vietnam's Sabeco.
markets: Sells in Thailand, Vietnam and Southeast Asia, with Scotch whisky and UK operations and exports to other regions.
rationale: Major Asian drinks group with sponsorship culture; rival Thai brand Singha is an F1 partner, so a direct fit exists.

name: Emperador
desc: Philippine alcoholic beverage company making Emperador Brandy and owning Whyte and Mackay Scotch whisky and Spanish brandies.
markets: Sells in the Philippines, Spain, the UK and other export markets through distributors.
rationale: Large brandy and whisky group with international growth; F1 gives global brand exposure, though alcohol rules vary by market.

name: Heritage Distilling
desc: Washington craft distillery making whiskey, vodka, gin and ready-to-drink cocktails sold mainly in the United States.
markets: Sells through its own tasting rooms and retailers in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small US craft distiller with limited budget and domestic distribution; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Pivoted to holding cryptocurrency after its 2024 Nasdaq listing

name: JIANGXIAOBAI
desc: Chinese baijiu brand launched in 2012 in Chongqing, selling light, youth-oriented sorghum liquor.
markets: Sold in China through retail and online channels; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Young-consumer baijiu brand with strong marketing but only Chinese sales; F1 fit is limited to China Grand Prix exposure.

name: Bira 91
desc: Indian craft beer brand from B9 Beverages selling Bira White, Blonde and other beers.
markets: Sells mainly in India through retail and taprooms, with some exports; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Youth-oriented craft beer brand with event marketing; India has no Grand Prix and alcohol advertising is restricted.

name: International Breweries
desc: Nigerian brewer with a main plant in Sapele, making and selling beers including Trophy, Hero and Budweiser.
markets: Brews and sells beers in Nigeria; owned by the Anheuser-Busch InBev group.
rationale: Nigerian brewer with a domestic market and sponsorship culture, but no Grand Prix and a parent that decides marketing.

name: Guanyun Liquor
desc: Beijing-based Chinese baijiu liquor company that brews and sells spirits; product range not confirmed from the input.
markets: Presumed customers in China; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Chinese liquor producer with unconfirmed scale and domestic focus; F1 fit is limited to China Grand Prix exposure.

name: Reed's
desc: Connecticut beverage company known for Reed's Ginger Beer, Virgil's sodas and Culture Club kombucha sold across the United States.
industry: craft soda and ginger beer maker
markets: Sells in US supermarkets and retailers through distributors; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small US premium soda brand with a limited marketing budget; F1 fit is weak.

name: Diamond Estates Wines & Spirits
desc: Canadian winery and spirits company based in Niagara-on-the-Lake producing and distributing wines and spirits.
markets: Sells in Canada through its own wineries and retail channels; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small Canadian wine and spirits maker with local distribution; F1 fit is weak despite the Canadian Grand Prix.

name: BrewDog
desc: Scottish craft brewer founded in 2007, making Punk IPA and other beers sold in shops and its own bars.
markets: Beers sold in the UK, Europe, the US and Australia, with breweries in Scotland, Ohio and Australia.
rationale: Brand-led craft brewer with event sponsorship record; no-alcohol lines and F1 fan culture suit a hospitality and activation tie-in.

name: Nigerian Breweries
desc: Nigeria's largest brewer, founded in 1946, making Star, Gulder and Heineken beers and malt drinks.
markets: Breweries and sales across Nigeria; majority-owned by Heineken.
rationale: Dominant Nigerian brewer with large consumer marketing, but no Grand Prix and a parent that already partners with F1.
f1: Majority-owned by Heineken N.V., a current F1 partner

name: Carlsberg Marston's
desc: UK brewer formed in 2020 as a joint venture, making Carlsberg, Tuborg, Banks's and Hobgoblin beers for pubs and shops.
markets: Beer supplied to British pubs, supermarkets and consumers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: British brewer with strong pub and sports sponsorship reach; British Grand Prix hospitality fits, but it is a domestic business.
changed: Formed in 2020 as a joint venture of Carlsberg and Marston's

name: Naked Wines
desc: Norwich online wine retailer that crowdfunds independent winemakers and sells their wines to subscribers.
markets: Customers in the UK, the United States and Australia through its online subscription membership model.
rationale: Online wine club with UK and US customers; F1 hospitality gives limited reach for a subscription business.

name: Piccadily Agro Industries
desc: Indian company running sugar mills, a distillery and bottling operations, selling Indri single malt whisky and other spirits.
markets: Sells sugar and spirits mainly in India; Indri single malt has won international awards.
rationale: Indian whisky maker with an awarded single malt brand; Indian alcohol advertising rules limit sponsorship, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Gong cha
desc: International bubble tea franchise from Taiwan selling milk teas, fruit teas and toppings through franchised shops.
markets: Franchised shops in about 25 countries across Asia, Oceania, Europe and North America.
rationale: Youth-oriented consumer franchise with global store network; F1 offers fan reach and promotions in many of its markets.

name: Sula Vineyards
desc: India's largest wine producer, making Sula, Rasa and Dindori wines and running vineyard tourism.
markets: Sells mainly in India with some exports; operates vineyard resorts near Nashik.
rationale: Leading Indian wine brand with lifestyle and tourism appeal; India has no Grand Prix and alcohol advertising is restricted.
